properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 9:52AM PST until November 2 at 9:15AM PST by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...South Central Mohave County in northwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1015 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1052 AM MST, Burro Creek at Highway 93 has recently risen to
17.4 feet, which is a record crest level. Trout Creek above
Knight Creek has also observed  sharp rises. Significant flooding
is expected on the Big Sandy near Wikieup, cresting above Major
Flood Stage. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the rivers...
Big Sandy River.
- For the Big Sandy at Wikieup:
At 9:30am the stage was 6.62 feet. Minor Flood Stage is 16.0
feet. Major Flood Stage is 18.0 feet.
Forecast: The river is forecast to crest around 3:00pm Sunday at
22.47 feet. This is above Major flood stage and near the record
flood stage of 22.4 feet set in February 1993.
Impacts:
At 16.0 feet: Minor flooding of low lying and remote areas near
the River basin are expected.
At 18.0 feet: Significant flooding of the adjacent river basin
and inundation of rural roadways near the basin floor.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wikieup.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Arizona, including mainly
Southern Gila County.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An atmospheric river ahead of a weather system will continue to
bring well above normal moisture to the region through today and
lead to a prolonged period of light to moderate rainfall across
the Watch area. Embedded convection will produce pockets of
heavier rain. Additional rainfall amounts, on the order of 1-2+",
through the course of Sunday on top of already moist soils, will
lead to additional runoff. Runoff in major streams, creeks, and
rivers may persist through the first half of the week.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 430 PM MST.

* At 1030 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the
warned area. Between 1.75 and 2.75 inches of rain have fallen.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

State Park, Indian Maiden Falls and West Clear Creek Wilderness.

Indian Maiden Falls.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Beaver Creek, West Clear Creek, Verde River, Fossil Creek, Walker
Creek, Bull Run Creek, Long Canyon and Russell Wash.

muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 8:49AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent east-northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the
St John River have slowed flow at Astor. Forecast rainfall may lead
to additional rises within Moderate flood stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 3.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Sunday was 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.4 feet
this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

through flooded areas.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northwest, and west central New
Mexico, including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,
Far Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands and
Tusas Mountains Including Chama. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska
Mountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico, San
Francisco River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central
Highlands, West Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of widespread rainfall is expected today into
Monday with rainfall amounts generally between 1 and 2 inches
near and west of the Continental Divide, except near 3 inches in

rainfall will occur over very saturated soils which will increase
runoff. These are also areas that are still recovering from the
last flood event. River rises are likely and some rivers may
flood. If river flooding materializes, it will likely continue
into Monday evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 5:48AM MST until November 3 at 2:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Animas River Near Cedar Hill affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...Animas River near Cedar Hill.

* WHEN...From Monday morning to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 11.5 feet, The river would be near an all time high.
Areas along the river that never before experienced flooding will
likely be inundated as water levels continue to rise.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 AM MST Sunday the stage was 7.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tonight to a crest of 11.1 feet early tomorrow afternoon. It will
then fall below flood stage late tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.9
feet on 05/14/1941.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 5:28AM MST until November 1 at 10:00PM MST by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall possible.

* WHERE...In Southwest New Mexico, Grant County, northern Hidalgo
County, and western Sierra County. This includes Silver City,
Lordsburg, Gila, and other surrounding communities. This includes
the Gila and upper Mimbres watersheds.

* WHEN...From noon MST today through late this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may become flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Pacific frontal boundary will move through New Mexico this
afternoon, bringing widespread showers and thunderstorms to much
of western New Mexico. Storms will be capable of heavy rain and
training, which will lead to localized flash flooding. High soil
saturation due to recent rains will cause runoff to occur more
quickly.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 5:05AM MST until November 1 at 2:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks and normally dry washes is imminent or
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 504 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 1 and 2.25 inches of rain have
fallen.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Coffee Creek, Sycamore Creek, Sinclair Wash, Spring Creek, Verde
River, Tule Tank Wash, West Fork Oak Creek, Oak Creek, Turkey
Creek, Bitter Creek, Blowout Creek, Pumphouse Wash, Bear Canyon,
Dry Creek, Railroad Draw, Dry Beaver Creek, Oak Wash, Volunteer
Wash and JD Dam Wash. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2
inches are possible in the warned area.
- For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 4:00am the stage was 2.67 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 11.91 feet is expected at 8:00pm Sunday.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Flooding begins to inundate lower terrace of RV park
upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge.
- For Oak Creek at Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 4:45am the stage was 8.65 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 13.94 feet is expected at 6:00pm Sunday.
Impacts:
At 5.0 feet: Multiple private low water crossings and bridges
over Oak Creek above Sedona become impassable.
At 7.0 feet: Likely to cause minor flooding downstream in Page
Springs area near stream gage OACA3 4 to 6 hours later.
- For Verde River at Verde River near Camp Verde:
At 4:00am the stage was 4.37 feet.
Flood Stage is 17.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 14.65 feet is expected at 12:00pm Monday.
- For Verde River at Clarkdale:
At 4:00am the stage was 2.81 feet.
Flood Stage is 12.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 9.98 feet is expected at 8:00am Monday.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Cottonwood, Sedona, Verde Village, Clarkdale, Cornville, Kachina

properties.description:

For the West Hobolochitto Creek...including McNeil...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHEN...From early this morning to Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, North Beech Road and Palestine Road in
Picayune will be impassable. Several homes will be flooded in
vicinity of the stream. Flooding threatens structures along MS
Highway 43 near the bridge and fills culverts and ditches along
bridge approach.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:45 AM CST Sunday the stage was 17.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:45 AM CST Sunday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.5 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.5
feet on 04/10/2021.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler and Southeast Coastal St. Johns
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20

falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
and dragging anchors.

vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Middle and Lower Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Saltwater flooding of low elevation streets and lots
is expected. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 1 at 1:48AM PDT until November 2 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...A high risk for sneaker waves is expected. A building
west-northwest long period swell is expected to combine with
lower, shorter period northwest and south-southwest swells.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These
waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and sweep
them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Avoid climbing on rocks and jetties. Stay away from the ocean and
remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 1 at 1:07AM PDT until November 3 at 8:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from late Sunday night
through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on
Sunday 11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5
ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 1 at 1:07AM PDT until November 1 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on
Sunday 11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5
ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:

areas, Hualapai Mountains, Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave, Lake Mead -
AZ side, Lake Mohave - AZ side, Northwest Deserts and Northwest
Plateau, southeast California, including the following area, San

including the following areas, Lake Mead - NV side, Lake Mohave -
NV side, Lincoln County and Northeast Clark County.

* WHEN...Now through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

inch and an inch of rain will be possible. With saturated soils
and significant run off expected, flash flooding  may occur.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 1 at 1:39AM EDT until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal portions of Saint Lucie and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory,
until 7 PM EST Monday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through
late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 31 at 10:07PM PDT until November 2 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Monday evening. .

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 11:03PM MDT until November 1 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef
National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake
Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread moderate to at times heavy precipitation is expected
across much of southern, southeast and east central Utah tonight
through Sunday.

Moist antecedent conditions from recent heavy rains will result
in efficient and excessive runoff, allowing all area washes,
streams and rivers to run fast and high. Flood prone areas will
likely become inundated at times, and backcountry roads will
likely become impassable from this excessive runoff.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

...A SPECIAL AVALANCHE ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 4:30 PM SATURDAY
UNTIL 4:30 PM MONDAY...

natural avalanches above treeline. Check the forecast at
www.colorado.gov/avalanche.

Beyer & Pritchett
